title: The helper that remembered too much
arc: Meridian's analysts share a file of helper functions, and one of them has started returning yesterday's results. The culprit is a default argument that is created once and shared forever. This week you make the helpers safe to reuse: closures that keep state on purpose, comprehensions where they help and loops where they don't, sorting by several keys, and a retry decorator Dev can put on flaky API calls. By Friday the shared file is something you would let a new hire use.

scenes.monday: Mei from finance asks why the refund report "remembers" refunds from the day before. You find a helper with a list as its default argument. Start with functions as values and the mutable default trap.
scenes.midweek: The payments partner's API fails one call in fifty. Dev has pasted try/except into nine places. Write one retry decorator instead, and decide which errors it should never retry.
scenes.friday: You turn the shared helpers into a small pipeline of pure functions, each tested on its own. Grace asks why pure functions matter in a data pipeline. Have an answer ready.
